conviction_note: No decisive unpriced number found. A slight up lean comes from the company's habit of beating its own revenue guide (Q2 2026 $143.1m against a $135-137m guide), the guided Q3 price increases and gross-margin lift, and a 10.7%-of-float short with 13 days to cover. Against that sit two proxies: China passenger-car retail fell 24-28% YoY in Aug-Sep 2026, and Tesla US sales fell about 26% YoY in August against the Q3 2025 tax-credit pull-forward. Both trends sit roughly inside the 'consistent trends' assumption behind the guide. So p_up is 53 on a 9.5% abs move (the name's own median reaction; the option chain is unusable at a 90% spread), which gives +0.57. The findings sum to +0.7. The two measurements agree in sign and size.
bar: Company guide: Q3 2026 revenue approx $137-139m (Q2 2026 8-K, 2026-08-05, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001767258/000176725826000071/xpelq22026earnings.htm), no EPS guide. Consensus is disputed: Benzinga lists Q3'26E revenue $138.4m and EPS $0.61 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/XPEL/earnings-forecasts); Chartmill on 2026-08-05 had the sales estimate at $141.3m (https://www.chartmill.com/news/XPEL/Chartmill-52812-XPEL-NASDAQXPEL-Tops-Q2-Estimates-Shares-Rise-Pre-Market); Earnings Whispers shows EPS $0.55 (undated). I sized against the guide midpoint, $138m, and roughly $138-141m consensus. Revenue estimate: ~$140-141m, i.e. about +1.5% against $138.4m.
positioning_check: Short interest 2.67M shares, 10.72% of float, 13.21 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-30, up 4.65% from the prior report (Chartmill via search snippet; the page itself returned 403: https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/XPEL/ownership/short-interest). Earlier readings: 8.55 DTC on 2026-03-13 (equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/xpel/shortinterest) and 10.2 DTC in Oct 2025 (MarketBeat). The short is crowded for a ~187k-share/day name, which gives a squeeze mechanism on an in-line or better print. Options: front expiry 2026-11-20, ATM IV 87.6%, 25d skew -15.26 vol points (calls richer, 'upside paid'), P/C OI ratio 46.7 on 4,195 total OI, ATM spread 90% of mid. The baseline marks the chain too wide to mean anything, so the skew is weak evidence. Tape: spot $42.84, -5.1% over 20 days, -22% from the 52-week high, +24% from the low.

findings.finding: XPEL beat its own revenue guide by a wide margin last quarter: Q2 2026 revenue was $143.1m against its own Q2 guide of approx $135-137m (+5.2% vs the $136m midpoint) and a $134.8-137.8m consensus. Q3 2025 also beat ($125.4m). The current Q3 guide of $137-139m sits at or just below consensus ($138.4m Benzinga; $141.3m Chartmill in August). If the company again clears its own range by a few percent, Q3 revenue lands near $141-145m, a beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue beat ($143.1m vs $134.8-137.8m) with a raised-looking Q3 guide: stock +9.54% (2026-08-05). Q3 2025 revenue beat, EPS miss: +0.94% (2025-11-05). Q1 2026 -11.83% and Q4 2025 -6.86% (causes not verified here). Beats have been bought when the guide holds.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus ($138.4m) sits at the guide midpoint rather than at the company's realised beat cadence. If the street were pricing the habitual beat, the estimate would sit near $142m and the stock would not be 22% off its high with a 10.7% short.
findings.independence: The Q2 2026 actual comes from a different document, the Q2 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001767258/000176725826000071/xpelq22026earnings.htm. Consensus figures: https://www.chartmill.com/news/XPEL/Chartmill-52812-XPEL-NASDAQXPEL-Tops-Q2-Estimates-Shares-Rise-Pre-Market

findings.finding: On the Q2 call management said gross margin should keep rising modestly through 2026 and that it would take modest price increases in some regions in Q3 to offset cost pressure. Q2 gross margin was 44.1% vs 42.9% a year earlier, and GM dollars grew +18.0% on +14.7% revenue. Q3 EPS consensus is $0.61 (Benzinga) against $0.68 adjusted in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 margin expansion (+120bp) came with a +9.54% reaction. Q3 2025's EPS miss despite a revenue beat came with only +0.94%, so the margin/EPS line matters on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced, because management said it in public. EPS consensus of $0.61 on ~$138m implies a step down from $0.68 on $143m that is larger than the revenue step alone would imply, so it does not visibly credit price increases plus margin lift. Manufacturing start-up costs (excluded from adjusted figures) could offset it.
findings.independence: Same call as the Q2 release. The GM figures come from the 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001767258/000176725826000071/xpelq22026earnings.htm. Note: my fetch of the MarketBeat page returned a feed index; the content is from the search-engine summary of that URL.

findings.finding: China passenger-car retail fell harder in Q3 2026: CPCA final September retail 1.618m units, -28.0% YoY, and August -24%. In Q2 2026, which already had weak domestic sales, May was -20% and June -23.2%. XPEL China was $15.9m in Q2 (+106.7%, 11% of revenue). Its YoY growth in Q3 still benefits from the distributor acquisition, which closed late in Q3 2025 (Q3 2025 China base $10.1m). The risk is sequential: China below ~$15m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved print turned visibly on China. On the Q2 2026 call management called China integration a positive despite weak domestic sales, and the stock rose +9.54%.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro proxy for 11% of revenue. The guide assumed 'consistent trends in APAC', and a slightly worse China market is only a few-point deterioration, which no estimate visibly reflects. Net of the rest: the US (55%) and Canada would have to hold ~11% growth for total revenue to clear the guide, and a $1-2m China shortfall is ~1% of revenue.
findings.independence: CPCA September preliminary -24% (SteelOrbis): https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-news/latest-news/cpca-chinas-passenger-vehicle-retail-sales-down-24-in-september-2026-1482872.htm. Q3 2025 China base: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1767258/000176725825000064/xpelq32025er.htm. All of this is a proxy; the company has not confirmed it.

findings.finding: Tesla is a large source of XPEL's US aftermarket PPF demand, and its US sales fell about 26% YoY in August 2026 (~40.8k units) against Q3 2025's record, which was boosted by the 2025-09-30 federal EV credit expiry. Tesla global Q3 2026 deliveries were 486,532, -2% YoY but above the 461,974 company-compiled consensus, helped by Shanghai exports. XPEL US grew +11.1% in Q3 2025 and +11.7% in Q2 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history. The US region is 55% of revenue, and its growth has been the stable core in every quarter cited here.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a counterparty proxy, and XPEL's US mix has diversified into dealership programs and window film (+16.1%). The street's Q3 estimate sits at the guide, which assumed 'consistent US trends' and was set after the credit had expired. A harder Tesla comp in Q3 than in Q2 is not visibly in the estimates. Sized small because XPEL has not confirmed the transmission.
findings.independence: Tesla Q3 deliveries: https://electrek.co/2026/10/02/tesla-q3-2026-deliveries-486532/. US Q3 2026 total light-vehicle sales -0.4% YoY (separate source): https://www.carpro.com/blog/national-sales-results-for-all-automakers-year-to-date-q3-2026

findings.finding: US new-vehicle sales were flat to slightly down in Q3 2026: Carpro reports Q3 -0.4% YoY and nine months -1.2%, and Mercer puts the September SAAR at ~16.0m, down from 16.6-16.8m in August, with affordability the constraint. That leaves the dealership channel without a tailwind.
findings.why_not_priced: Flat industry volume matches the 'consistent US trends' behind the guide, so it is inside the guide and near zero.

findings.finding: Europe faces a hard comp: EU/UK/Africa revenue was $16.5m in Q3 2025, +28.8% YoY, while Q2 2026 EU was $17.0m, -2.3% YoY. Management flagged European seasonality and continued Europe and Middle East weakness in the Q3 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 printed EU -2.3% and India/ME -5.0%, and the stock still rose +9.54%. Weak regions have been looked through when the total beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, because the company guided to it explicitly. Filed because a negative EU YoY print in Q3 will be visible in the release table.

findings.finding: The short is crowded into the print: 2.67m shares, 10.72% of float, 13.21 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement, up 4.65% from the prior period, on a stock 22% off its 52-week high and -5% over 20 days. An in-line or better print against a guide-level bar gives shorts a reason to cover over 13 days of volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat came with +9.54% and Q1 2025 with +14.41%: large up moves on good prints are consistent with short covering. Down moves of -11.8% and -14.6% show the asymmetry runs both ways.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the market's own bet rather than a mispricing, so this is a mechanism and not information. Sized small. It amplifies whichever sign the guide gives.
findings.independence: Earlier trend in days to cover (8.55 on 2026-03-13): https://equibles.com/stocks/xpel/shortinterest. The option chain's call skew (-15.3 vol points) points the same way but is unreliable at a 90% spread.

outside_window.finding: Manufacturing margin benefits from the San Antonio and China facilities are guided to begin mid-2027, with a mid-20% operating-margin run rate targeted by end-2028. This is relevant to the multiple but not to this print.

Q4 2026 guide expectations: Benzinga Q4'26E $132.9m. No company or peer datapoint found that tests it.
Window-film or PPF peer prints after 2026-08-05: no listed direct peer found.
Option chain: unusable (90% ATM spread), so no implied move.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Tesla global Q3 2026 deliveries beat consensus (486.5k vs 462.0k), read as a positive for XPEL
rejected_candidates.detail: Merged into the Tesla US sales finding. The beat came from Shanghai exports, while the US channel XPEL serves fell, so it is one fact with one net sign.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Q2 2026 cash used in investing of $72.9m (capex $65.1m for San Antonio and China plants), read as financing or balance-sheet strain
rejected_candidates.detail: The same 8-K and the 2026-05-19 release show the spend is the announced ~$110m manufacturing programme, inside the stated $75-150m range. That makes it funded expansion, not distress, and worth ~0 to this print.

baseline_tension: Roughly agrees with the baseline: the tape is -5% over 20 days and -22% off the high, the unreliable option skew leans to calls, and the short is crowded. My slight up lean is small and partly the same positioning fact, so it adds little beyond the price.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): China proxy -0.7 -> -0.5 and Tesla US proxy -0.8 -> -0.6, given 10.7% of float short and 13 days to cover.
Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): China finding rewritten net of the 89% of revenue outside China. It stays small.

Lessons 6 and 1 (bar and reaction): the bar is the company guide since consensus disputes it ($138.4m vs $141.3m). The beat-pattern finding was left at +1.0 because this name bought its last beat (+9.5%).
Lesson 8 and the core (hunters undersize): abs_move_pct raised from 9.0 to 9.5, the name's own median reaction. p_up unchanged at 53.
